newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt 1996 accounts $3.6 billion in positive - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt 1996 accounts $3.6 billion in positive - SNZ.

text.p: New Zealand government accounts after financing its current and capital expenditure were positive to the tune of $3.61 billion, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
Deputy government statistician Ian Ewing said the accounts were an alternative economic analysis based on the New Zealand System of National Accounts of the government Financial Statements.
Total current income rose by $1.48 billion, 4.6 percent, to $33.58 billion.
Taxes contributed $1.97 billion to the increase with direct taxes up $1.38 billion.
The increase in taxes was offset by a fall dividends and profits of $514 million, mainly due to lower dividends from State-Owned Enterprises.
Current and capital expenditure by government, excluding major projects refinancing, increased by $964 million, 3.3 percent, to $29.98 billion.
Spending on social welfare accounted for 38.3 percent of total spending, followed by health services, 15.6 percent, education, 14.5 percent and debt servicing, 11.9 percent.
Debt servicing was the only significant fall in spending, down $199 million, with $243 less paid in foreign currency and $44 million more paid in New Zealand dollars.
